title: Wage growth holds at 3.7% — but real wages are finally ahead of inflation again
excerpt: The Wage Price Index rose 3.7% over the year to the June quarter, the same as March. With inflation now at 2.7%, real wages are growing for the fourth quarter in a row.
body:
Australian wages grew 3.7% over the year to the June quarter, unchanged from the March print, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics Wage Price Index released this week. The result was a touch softer than the 3.8% economists had forecast.

Public-sector wages rose 4.1%, the fastest of any sector, driven by ongoing state government enterprise bargaining agreements. Private-sector wages grew 3.6% — the slowest since late 2022.

The more important number is what it means in real terms. With CPI inflation at 2.7%, real wages are now growing at about 1.0% per year. For a worker on $85,000, that is roughly an extra $850 in real spending power over a year — small, but the fourth consecutive quarter of positive real-wage growth.
whatItMeans: Most workers: Your next pay rise will likely be in the 3.5–4.0% range if you ask. Anything under 3% in 2026 is effectively a pay cut after inflation.
Public-sector workers: Your EBAs are delivering the strongest wage growth. If you are a teacher, nurse, or public servant mid-agreement, you are getting above-inflation pay rises built in.
Hiring managers: Labour costs are still rising faster than pre-pandemic norms. Budget 4% wage growth into 2026 forecasts.
RBA: A 3.7% wage growth print is consistent with the RBA's view that the labour market is still tight enough to keep services inflation sticky. Reduces the case for an early cut.
